source.author: Al Brooks
source.chapter_title: First Pullback Sequence: Bar, Minor Trend Line, Moving Average, Moving Average Gap, Major Trend Line

conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode

candidates.name: ShrinkingBullBodies
candidates.quote: The bull bodies become smaller.
candidates.description: Shared primitive, stage 1 of the bull-trend weakening sequence: the current bull bar's body is smaller than the prior bull bar's body.
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] > open[0] && close[1] > open[1] && (close[0] - open[0]) < (close[1] - open[1])
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context signal, not itself an order)

complexity.reason: two-bar body comparison

notes: First of an explicit 22-item ordered checklist (pp. 90-91) of bull-trend weakening signs; the bear-trend version is given verbatim as a mirror in the text.

candidates.name: GrowingTopTails
candidates.quote: Tails start to form on the tops of bars, and the tails become larger on subsequent bars.
candidates.description: Stage 2: a bar has a nonzero top tail, and the top tail grows larger than the prior bar's top tail.
candidates.pseudocode: topTail0 = high[0] - max(open[0], close[0]); topTail1 = high[1] - max(open[1], close[1]); topTail0 > 0 && topTail0 > topTail1

complexity.reason: two-bar tail-size comparison

candidates.name: IncreasingBarOverlap
candidates.quote: Bars overlap their respective prior bars more than they did earlier.
candidates.description: Stage 3: the current bar's overlap with the prior bar (as a fraction of the prior bar's range) exceeds the overlap fraction measured lagBars earlier.
candidates.pseudocode: overlap0 = (min(high[0], high[1]) - max(low[0], low[1])) / (high[1] - low[1]); overlapLag = (min(high[lagBars], high[lagBars+1]) - max(low[lagBars], low[lagBars+1])) / (high[lagBars+1] - low[lagBars+1]); overlap0 > overlapLag

complexity.reason: two two-bar overlap ratios compared

candidates.name: SmallBodyOrDojiBar
candidates.quote: A bar has a very small body or a doji body.
candidates.description: Stage 4: the current bar's body is a small fraction of its own range.

complexity.reason: single-bar body arithmetic

notes: Same shape as R08-03's DojiBar with a looser threshold.

candidates.name: OppositeColorBar
candidates.quote: A bar has a bear body.
candidates.description: Stage 5: the current bar closes against the prevailing trend's color (a bear body in a bull trend).

complexity.reason: single-bar comparison

candidates.name: HighAtOrBelowPriorHigh
candidates.quote: The high of the current bar is at or below the high of prior bar.
candidates.description: Stage 6: the current bar fails to make a new high.

complexity.reason: two-bar comparison

candidates.name: LowNearOrAbovePriorLow
candidates.quote: The low of the current bar is at or just above the low of prior bar.
candidates.description: Stage 7: the current bar's low sits at or only a few ticks above the prior bar's low.
candidates.pseudocode: low[0] >= low[1] && low[0] <= low[1] + nearTicks * tickSize

complexity.reason: two-bar comparison with a tick tolerance

candidates.name: LowBelowPriorLow
candidates.quote: The low of the current bar is below the low of the prior bar.
candidates.description: Stage 8: the current bar makes a new low relative to the prior bar -- the first true pullback bar.

complexity.reason: two-bar comparison

notes: Same shape as RP3-01 (PullbackBarStrict) but without the one-tick buffer; the dedup pass should reconcile the two.

candidates.name: OneLeggedPullbackHigh1
candidates.quote: There is a one-legged pullback (a high 1 buy setup), where the high of the bar is below the high of the prior bar.
candidates.description: The first, mildest pullback type: a single pullback bar whose high stays below the prior bar's high; buy a stop above its high.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the pullback bar's high

complexity.reason: single two-bar comparison

notes: Called the 'high 1' setup; formalized in full in Chapter 17. Same shape as RP3-08's pause-bar entry, recorded here from its own explicit definition.

candidates.name: AggressiveLimitEntryBelowPullbackLow
candidates.quote: Aggressive traders will buy on a limit order below the low of the prior bar, expecting the pullback to be brief and wanting to get in at a lower price than the traders who are waiting to buy on a stop above the pullback bar or bars.
candidates.description: Aggressive alternative to R11-09: during a one-legged pullback, rest a limit buy a few ticks below the prior (pre-pullback) bar's low instead of waiting for the stop entry above the pullback bar's high.
candidates.pseudocode: limitPrice = low[1] - limitOffsetTicks * tickSize; low[0] <= limitPrice  (fill assumed when the pullback bar trades down to the limit)
candidates.book_order_type: limit order below the low of the bar before the pullback

complexity.reason: an intrabar limit-fill assumption rather than a close-based test

candidates.name: TwoLeggedPullbackHigh2WithDuration
candidates.quote: There is a two-legged pullback (a high 2 buy setup) lasting only five to about 10 bars.
candidates.description: A two-legged pullback (ABC / high 2) whose total duration falls within a book-typical range of bars.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the second leg's reversal bar

complexity.reason: inherits TwoLeggedPullback's unresolved leg-counting design decision

candidates.name: ThreeLeggedPullbackWedgeOrTriangle
candidates.quote: There is a three-legged pullback (a wedge bull flag or a triangle) lasting only five to about 15 bars.
candidates.description: A three-legged pullback forming a wedge bull flag or triangle, lasting within a book-typical bar range.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the third push's reversal bar

complexity.reason: three-push wedge/triangle recognition over a variable-length window; developed further in Chapter 18

candidates.name: MinorTrendLineBreak
candidates.quote: There is a break of a minor bull trend line.
candidates.description: The current bar closes beyond a minor trend line (drawn through the two most recent, closely spaced swing lows in a bull trend).
candidates.pseudocode: minorTrendLine = line through the last two swing lows within minorLookback bars; close[0] < minorTrendLine[0]
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context signal; often traded as a breakout-pullback setup)

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection and trend-line projection

candidates.name: MovingAverageTouchGapBarSetup
candidates.quote: A bar touches the moving average (a 20 gap bar buy setup).
candidates.description: The current bar's low touches or dips into the 20-bar EMA after a pullback, a classic support test (the '20 gap bar' setup, developed fully in Chapter 13).
candidates.pseudocode: low[0] <= ema(emaLength)[0] && low[0] >= ema(emaLength)[0] - touchTicks * tickSize
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the touch bar's high

complexity.reason: needs the EMA plus a touch-tolerance test

candidates.name: RallyToNewHighContainsOppositeColorBars
candidates.quote: The next rally to a new high has one or more bear trend bars and a pullback or two.
candidates.description: Stage marker: the leg that makes the next new high itself contains one or more opposite-color (bear) trend bars, a sign the trend is weakening even while still making progress.

complexity.reason: needs the current leg's start to persist plus a count over it

candidates.name: CloseBelowMovingAverage
candidates.quote: A bar has a close below the moving average.
candidates.description: Stage marker: a bar closes below the 20-bar EMA in an established bull trend, deeper than a mere touch.

complexity.reason: single EMA comparison

candidates.name: MovingAverageGapBar
candidates.quote: A bar has a high below the moving average (a moving average gap bar).
candidates.description: Shared primitive: the entire bar (its high, not just the close) sits below the 20-bar EMA -- a moving-average gap bar, a materially deeper sign of weakness than CloseBelowMovingAverage.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context signal, often the first leg toward a major trend-line break)

complexity.reason: single EMA comparison

notes: Same construction as R08-25's EmaGapBarAsCountertrendStrength; here it is one stage in a bull trend's own weakening sequence rather than a countertrend-permission filter.

candidates.name: MajorTrendLineBreak
candidates.quote: There is a break of a major bull trend line.
candidates.description: The current bar closes beyond a major trend line -- drawn through swing lows spanning a much longer lookback than MinorTrendLineBreak, marking the more significant weakening stage.
candidates.pseudocode: majorTrendLine = line through the last two swing lows within majorLookback bars; close[0] < majorTrendLine[0]
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context signal; often precedes a two-legged countertrend move or reversal)

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection and trend-line projection; 'major' vs 'minor' is a lookback/pivot-strength design choice

candidates.name: SecondLegDownAfterMaGapBarBeforeReclaim
candidates.quote: Once there is a bar with a high below the moving average, there is a second leg down before the market gets back above the moving average.
candidates.description: Filter/expectation: after the first MovingAverageGapBar, expect a second down-leg before the market reclaims the EMA -- caution against expecting an immediate with-trend resumption.

complexity.reason: needs leg counting after the gap bar, same unresolved design decision as elsewhere

candidates.name: MultiplePullbacksInFinalRallyWithOppositeBodies
candidates.quote: The rally to the new high has two or more pullbacks, each lasting two or three bars and having more prominent bear bodies.
candidates.description: Stage marker: the final rally to a new extreme contains two or more short pullbacks (2-3 bars each) with increasingly prominent opposite-color bodies -- a late-stage weakening sign.

complexity.reason: needs pullback segmentation within a persisted leg

candidates.name: LargerTwoLeggedPullbackFormsLowerLow
candidates.quote: There is a larger two-legged pullback, lasting more than 10 bars, with the second leg down falling below a prominent higher low, forming a lower low.
candidates.description: A late-stage, longer two-legged pullback (>10 bars) whose second leg breaks below the most recent prominent higher low, printing the trend's first lower low.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context signal; the classic bull-to-trading-range transition marker)

complexity.reason: needs the remembered prior higher low plus leg-counting

candidates.name: TradingRangeEquilibriumBullBearBalance
candidates.quote: The market enters a trading range, and the bull and bear bars are about equally prominent.
candidates.description: Final stage marker: price is in a trading range and the counts/sizes of bull and bear bars over the range are roughly balanced -- the hallmark that the trend has stalled into two-sided trading.

complexity.reason: depends on a trading-range detector, itself a design decision as in the MINING brief's own example

candidates.name: FailedRangeBreakoutFormsLargerRange
candidates.quote: The market breaks above the trading range and comes back into the trading range, forming a larger trading range.
candidates.description: The final weakening stage: a breakout above the trading range fails and price re-enters the range, expanding it -- the clearest sign the trend has converted into a trading range.
candidates.pseudocode: close[b] > rangeHigh (breakout bar b) && close[0] < rangeHigh && (0 - b) <= reentryWindow

complexity.reason: needs the persisted range boundary and breakout bar plus a re-entry window

candidates.name: SuspiciousOfRepeatedHigh1AfterHigh2
candidates.quote: If the market went from one or two high 1 entries and then a high 2 entry, and it appeared to be setting up another high 1, it is wise to wait. After a series of winning trades, you should be suspicious of renewed strength without first seeing a larger pullback, since this strength might be a trap setting up.
candidates.description: Filter: withhold a fresh high-1 entry that follows an already-completed high-1(s)-then-high-2 sequence without an intervening larger pullback, since it may be a final-flag trap.
candidates.pseudocode: setupSequence == [H1(,H1), H2, H1] (most recent three-to-four with-trend setups) -> suppress this H1 entry

complexity.reason: needs the strategy to remember a sequence of prior setup TYPES, not just prices -- a new kind of state

notes: References the 'final flag' concept, developed in book 3.

candidates.name: MaTouchFailureExpectsDeeperPullback
candidates.quote: If the market cannot move above the moving average after about 10 to 20 bars, it is probably because traders want more of a discount before aggressively buying. The result is that the market will have to fall further before enough buyers return to lift the market up to test the old highs.
candidates.description: Filter: once price has failed to reclaim the EMA within N bars of touching it, withhold with-trend long entries and expect a deeper pullback before the old high is tested.

complexity.reason: needs the persisted bar count since the MA was first touched

candidates.name: TradingRangeEntryNearRangeExtremeOnly
candidates.quote: In a bull trend, you can buy if there is a setup near the low of the range, but be careful buying a breakout of the high of the trading range, because bears might be willing to sell a new high and bulls might be beginning to take profits at the high. ... if there is a short setup near the top of the flag, your risk is small and the trade is worth taking.
candidates.description: Filter: inside a trading range/flag that formed after a run of winning with-trend trades, permit a with-trend entry only near the range's far (trend-origin) extreme, not on a breakout of its near (trend-direction) extreme.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context filter on where within the range to enter)

complexity.reason: depends on a trading-range/flag detector

candidates.name: IncreasingMovingAveragePenetrationAcrossPullbacks
candidates.quote: Compare the bars 4, 5, and 8 tests of the moving average and notice that bar 5 penetrated it more than bar 4, and bar 8 had more penetration than bar 5. This is to be expected, and when this is the case be careful about placing a short trade, because there will be many smart bears who will short only at a higher price, and many bulls who will be confident enough to buy dips.
candidates.description: Filter: if each successive pullback penetrates the moving average more deeply than the last, be cautious about fading (countertrend) that penetration -- successive with-trend traders are buying dips more confidently and countertrend entries there carry more risk.

complexity.reason: needs the depth of the prior EMA-touch to persist across bars for comparison

candidates.name: HigherTimeframeSequentialMovingAveragePullback
candidates.quote: there is often a tendency for the first pullback to the 15 minute moving average to be followed by a test of the trend extreme, and then a pullback to the 30 or 60 minute moving average, which would likely be followed by another test of the extreme.
candidates.description: Higher-timeframe EMAs (15/30/60 minute) act as a sequence of successively larger magnets: the first pullback to reach a given higher-timeframe EMA is usually followed by a trend-extreme test, then the next pullback tests the next-larger timeframe's EMA.
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] within touchTicks of higherTfEma(emaLength, timeframeMinutes)[0]

complexity.reason: needs a design decision on whether/how the engine exposes a resampled higher-timeframe EMA, same as R10-16

notes: Brooks: not worth the effort on lower timeframes generally, but the tendency exists; kept low-confidence.

rejected.quote: The pullbacks don't have to occur in the exact same order. For example, sometimes a high 1 will occur after a high 2 if the trend accelerated after the high 2.
rejected.reason: meta-commentary on the ordering of the checklist items, not itself a decidable condition

rejected.quote: It is better to wait for more price action and miss a possible trap than to feel invincible and fearless because you fooled yourself into believing that you are playing with someone else's money.
rejected.reason: pure trading psychology, no bar-level test

rejected.quote: Although it is not worth the effort to pay attention to higher time frame charts when trading on a 5 minute chart, it is likely that the larger 5 minute pullbacks end at 15, 30, or 60 minute, or even daily, weekly, or monthly chart points of significance
rejected.reason: discretionary cost/benefit judgment about analysis effort, not a bar-level test; the underlying magnet claim is captured in R11-28

rejected.quote: Figure 11.1 ... Figure 11.2 ... Bar 1 was a two-legged higher high after a bull trend line break ... Bar 4 was a trend channel line overshoot
rejected.reason: worked chart examples narrating the already-recorded sequence items and prior primitives (two-bar reversal, breakout pullback, double top, double bottom bull flag) with specific bar numbers; no additional mechanical content

chapter_summary: The chapter's spine is two verbatim, mirror-image 22-item checklists (bull-trend and bear-trend) of ever-deepening signs of trend weakness, from shrinking bodies and growing tails through bar-overlap growth, doji/opposite-color bars, one/two/three-legged pullbacks (high 1/2/3), minor and major trend-line breaks, moving-average touches/closes/gap bars, and finally a trading range with balanced bull/bear bars that fails to hold a breakout. Each stage is recorded as its own primitive/context candidate (R11-01..R11-23), since the book explicitly treats each as an independently checkable, ordered signal (though not required to occur strictly in order). Surrounding prose adds a handful of standalone filters: suspicion of a repeated high-1 after a high-2 (final-flag trap), withholding longs when the market fails to reclaim the EMA quickly, entering a range only near its far extreme, watching for increasing EMA-penetration depth across successive pullbacks, and a higher-timeframe EMA pullback sequence. Figures 11.1 and 11.2 are worked examples of already-recorded patterns and contributed no new candidates.
